newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian tycoon wins Fergie for Opera Ball.
newsitem.headline: Austrian tycoon wins Fergie for Opera Ball.

text.p: Austrian tycoon Richard Lugner was savouring his triumph on Friday after Britain's Duchess of York, Sarah Ferguson, accepted his invitation as guest of honour to Vienna's prestigious Opera Ball.
"She was my first choice," Lugner told the current affairs magazine News.

Lugner, whose search for a companion for the ball each year stirs up a flurry of speculation in the Austrian media, has in the past been accompanied by actresses Sophia Loren, Bo Derek, socialite Ivana Trump and singer Grace Jones.

U.S. actress and singer Barbara Streisand was said to be his second choice as this year's guest but his heart was set on the flame-haired duchess, popularly known as "Fergie" and former wife of Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew.
Lugner, who reportedly paid one million schillings ($87,000) for the pleasure of Loren's company, declined to say how much he had forked out for Fergie.
"I am not paying in pennies," the magnate, who made his fortune in the construction industry, told Der Standard daily.
Austrian gossip columns have put the price paid by Lugner for the privilege of having Fergie on his arm at between 750,000 and 1.5 million schillings.

Lugner, ridiculed in Austrian society as a flashy parvenu, openly courts media attention, appearing flanked by glamorous women to promote his marketing strategies. He told News that no depths were too low for him.

The stocky tycoon will meet Fergie on her arrival from New York on February 6 and whisk her away by stretch limousine to the shopping complex "Lugner City," where she will sign copies of her autobiography "My Story."

"Fergie's doing it all herself. She's booking her flight, organising a three-room suite and I'll pick up the tab," Lugner said. "She's earning her pay for the hour of signing, not for the opera ball," he added.

Fergie, whose mounting debts have been well-publicised in the media, this month struck lucrative deals to advertise cranberry juice on television and to be spokeswoman for Weight Watchers International.

"It wasn't the question of money that delayed the negotiations for so long," Lugner told Die Presse. Security, a bad press and the other names on the guest list were the main concerns of the duchess, he said.
